V.}}</noinclude>{{dropinitial|A|fl={{verse|chapter=5|verse=1}}}}{{sc|Nd}} they came beyond the straite of the sea into the countrie of the Gerasens.{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Mat. 8, 28. Luc. 8, 26.''}} {{verse|chapter=5|verse=2}}† And as he vvent out of the boate, immediatly there mette him out of the sepulchres a man in an vncleane spirit, {{verse|chapter=5|verse=3}}† that had his dvvelling in the sepulchres. and neither vvith chaines {{sup|‖}} could any man novv binde him: {{verse|chapter=5|verse=4}}† for being often bound vvith fetters and chaines, he had burst the chaines, and broken the fetters. and no body could tame him. {{verse|chapter=5|verse=5}}† and he vvas alvvaies day and night in the sepulchres and in the mountaines, crying and cutting him self vvith stones. {{verse|chapter=5|verse=6}}† And seeing {{sc|Iesvs}} a farre of, he ranne and adored him: {{verse|chapter=5|verse=7}}† and crying vvith a great voice, said, What to me and thee {{sc|Iesvs}} the sonne of God most high? I adiure thee by God that thou torment me not. {{verse|chapter=5|verse=8}}† For he said vnto him, Goe out of the man thou vncleane spirit. {{verse|chapter=5|verse=9}}† And he asked him, What is thy name? And he saith to him, My name is Legion: because vve are many. {{verse|chapter=5|verse=10}}† And he besought him much, that he vvould not expel him out of the countrie. {{verse|chapter=5|verse=11}}† And there vvas there about the mountaine a great heard of svvine, feeding. {{verse|chapter=5|verse=12}}† And the spirits besought him, saying, Send vs {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ It is not with out mysterie that the diuels desired, and Christ suffered them to enter into the swine, signifying that filthy liuers be meete dwelling places for diuels. ''Aug. tract. 6 in ep. Io''.}}∷ into the svvine, that vve may enter into them. {{verse|chapter=5|verse=13}}† And {{sc|Iesvs}} immediatly graunted vnto them. And the vncleane spirits going out, entred into the svvine: and the heard vvith great violence vvas caried headlong into the sea, about tvvo thousand, and vvere stifled in the sea. {{verse|chapter=5|verse=14}}† And they that fed them, fled, and caried nevves into the citie and into the fields. And they vvent forth to see vvhat vvas done: {{verse|chapter=5|verse=15}}† and they come to {{sc|Iesvs}}, and they see him that vvas vexed of the deuil, sitting, clothed, and vvel in his vvittes: and they vvere afraid. {{verse|chapter=5|verse=16}}† And they that had seen it, told them, in vvhat maner he had been dealt vvithal that had the diuel: and of the swine. {{verse|chapter=5|verse=17}}† And they began to desire him, that he vvould depart from their coastes. {{verse|chapter=5|verse=18}}† And vvhen he vvent vp into the boate, he that had been vexed of the diuel, began to beseeche him that he might be vvith him, {{verse|chapter=5|verse=19}}† and he admitted him not, but saith to him, Goe into thy house to thine, and tel them hovv great things the Lord hath done for thee, and hath had mercie vpon thee. {{verse|chapter=5|verse=20}}† And he vvent his vvay, and began to publish in Decapolis hovv great things {{sc|Iesvs}} had done to him: and al marueled.<noinclude>{{rh|||And}}</noinclude>
